name: US inflation
summary: US CPI 4.0% y/y in September; October data due 10 Nov
state: Headline CPI rose 4.0% in the year to September, up from 3.7%, inside the 3–4.5% Watch band (BLS via FRED). Brent rebounded on 5 Nov from a two-month low near $94 as uncertainty over the Iran war persisted (The National), so energy prices remain a risk to the October figure, due on 10 Nov.
for_you: Higher prices for fuel, food and services squeeze household budgets; mortgage and loan rates tend to stay high while inflation is above target.

sources.title: FRED — CPI for all urban consumers
The National — Oil rebounds from two-month low as uncertainty lingers over Iran war

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
